body.statement: There exists a finite-alphabet model \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) whose graph and target data equal \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\). For every such faithful model, \(A(\eta^\dagger)=\{1\}\), \(Z_1=\{3\}\), and Dai et al.'s retained-edge result gives \(1\to2\) in \(M_1(\eta^\dagger)\). Consequently, the endpoint at vertex \(2\) on that retained adjacency is an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\). The corrected endpoint frontier therefore makes its arrowhead equivalence only for intervention-created adjacencies \(uv\notin H\); it makes no target-membership equivalence for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
body.justification: The explicit three-variable reduction separates retained basal orientation from the target-driven orientation mechanism and removes the failed normalization.
body.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 6 on p. 7, supplies retained-edge semantics; target membership controls intervention-created adjacencies through a distinct mechanism and cannot characterize retained-edge arrowheads.
body.consumer: It gives an executable unit check for any implementation of the fixed-selected-set endpoint frontier.
body.proof_tex:
Work against the corrected construction in \(\mathrm{def:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}specification}\), in which the selection edge is \(1\to s\).  Take all variables binary.  Let \(X_1\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and, conditionally on \(X_1\), set
\[
\Pr(X_2=X_1\mid X_1)=\frac34,
\qquad
\Pr(X_2\ne X_1\mid X_1)=\frac14.
\tag{1}
\]
For the selection vertex use the strictly positive kernel
\[
\Pr(S_s^*=1\mid X_1=x_1)=\frac12
\quad\text{for both }x_1\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Finally take \(X_3\) independent of the first component, with
\[
\Pr(X_3=1\mid \text{regime }0)=\frac14,
\qquad
\Pr(X_3=1\mid \text{regime }1)=\frac34.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) factorize over the graph in \(\mathrm{def:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}specification}\); the only kernel changed in regime \(1\) is that of the direct target \(3\).  The noises can be chosen independent, so causal sufficiency holds, and (2) gives \(\Pr(S^*=1)=1/2>0\).  The graph is acyclic, its selection vertex is childless, and its only selection parent is observed.  Thus every graphical, factorization, positivity, pre-treatment, and soft-intervention condition in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) holds.

Conditioning on \(S_s^*=1\) does not alter the law of \((X_1,X_2,X_3)\).  Under the pooled law,
\[
P_{\eta^\dagger,1}^{\mathrm{pool}}(x_1,x_2,x_3,z)
=P_{12}(x_1,x_2)\,
  \frac12 P_{3,z}(x_3),
\tag{4}
\]
where \(P_{12}\) is the table in (1), \(P_{3,0}(1)=1/4\), and \(P_{3,1}(1)=3/4\).  The two factors in (4) are independent components.  Each of the two binary \(2\)-by-\(2\) tables on \((X_1,X_2)\) and \((\zeta_1,X_3)\) has nonzero determinant: for the first, \(P(X_1=X_2)=3/4\ne1/2\), and for the second the two conditional success probabilities in (3) differ.  Consequently neither edge's endpoints become independent after conditioning on variables in the other component, while every cross-component conditional independence holds by the product in (4).  This is exactly faithfulness to the disjoint union of the single edges supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\).  Hence \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\).

The only parent of selection is \(1\), so
\[
A(\eta^\dagger)
=\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta^\dagger)}(\{1\})\cap V
=\{1\}.
\tag{5}
\]
The target \(3\) has no observed descendants other than itself, so the indicator-neighbor formula gives
\[
Z_1=T_1\cup
  \bigl((F_1\setminus T_1)\cap A(\eta^\dagger)\bigr)
=\{3\}.
\tag{6}
\]
In the observational MAG, the endpoint at \(1\) is a tail because \(1\in A(\eta^\dagger)\), while the endpoint at \(2\) is an arrowhead because \(2\notin A(\eta^\dagger)\) and \(2\notin\operatorname{An}_{G_0}(1)\).  Thus the observational edge is \(1\to2\), and it is retained in the regime MAG by the retained-directed-edge clause of the cited interface.  Its endpoint at \(2\) is therefore an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\) by (6).  This explicit member proves that target membership cannot characterize arrowheads on retained adjacencies. \(\square\)
